findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a gitlink 'sentry-repo' submodule at the repository root pointing to commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a with no .gitmodules entry and no justification anywhere in the PR. Every clone/CI checkout fails or silently materializes a broken submodule reference; there is no submodule configuration for this path, so 'git submodule update' errors out and the checkout is dirty in all environments.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to 'upsampled_count() as count', whose SnQLFunction aggregates Column('sample_weight'), a column that nothing in this diff (or any referenced migration/schema) defines on the errors dataset. The rewritten Snuba query references a nonexistent sample_weight column and fails with an invalid-column error at query time, so any request against an allowlisted org gets a 500 from the events-stats endpoint instead of data.

[BUG] test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects asserts data[i][1][0]['count'] == 10, but no code path in the diff computes or populates sample_weight — the factory change in tests/sentry/testutils/factories.py only sets a 'sample_rate' key on normalized_data, never a sample_weight column in Snuba. The test fails: the upsampled_count() function either errors (missing column) or sums nothing, so the expected 10 (1 event / 0.1 sample rate) never materializes; the PR's headline feature is untested against reality.

[BUG] The cache key is built with Python's built-in hash() ('...{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}'), which is salted per-process under PYTHONHASHSEED randomization. Different sentry-web/worker processes compute different cache keys for identical project sets, so the 60s cache and invalidate_upsampling_cache (same hash construction) never target the same key across processes — the invalidation is a silent no-op in any multi-process deployment and allowlist changes take effect inconsistently.

[BUG] _are_all_projects_error_upsampled reads options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist'), an option that is not registered in this diff and has no default definition shown, and compares project_ids with 'in' against the raw option value. If the option is not registered in the options registry, options.get raises (option does not exist), crashing every events-stats request for that org; even if registered elsewhere as a string set, 'project_id in allowlist' does int-vs-string comparison that never matches, silently disabling the feature.

[BUG] test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist and test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects do not clear the 60-second eligibility cache written by test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects, and cache.set is not mocked in these tests. In the default in-memory test cache, if the same organization/project ids recur (test DB sequences don't reset within a run), the cached eligibility from the earlier mocked-options test leaks in and the partial-allowlist request is upsampled, making the asserted count of 1 actually 10 and the test flaky-to-failing.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses substring matching, so the negated query '!event.type:error' is classified as error-focused and gets upsampled_count applied to a query explicitly excluding errors. A user querying `!event.type:error` on the discover dataset with allowlisted projects gets sum(sample_weight) instead of count() for non-error events; sample_weight doesn't exist on transactions, so the query errors or returns wrong counts.

[BUG] The eligibility cache key omits both the dataset and the request query, but the cached-True branch recomputes _should_apply_sample_weight_transform while the whole eligibility (including org membership) is frozen for 60s — more importantly, cache.get returning cached True bypasses nothing dataset-related correctly, but a cached eligibility computed for one project-id set is reused across any two requests in the org whose sorted project_ids collide after hash(), including requests from different organizations' users sharing the same org id — the real dropped requirement is that `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in this diff. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, all org queries for that project set keep returning upsampled (10x-inflated) counts for up to 60 seconds with no invalidation path; the function exists but no option-change hook, signal handler, or code path invokes it, so it is dead code.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites top-level y-axis columns exactly equal to 'count()', silently dropping the upsampled treatment for equations containing count() (e.g. yAxis 'equation|count()*2') and for count()-with-args variants. A dashboard widget whose y-axis is an equation referencing count() shows unsampled counts next to a sibling count() series that shows upsampled counts, producing internally inconsistent charts in the same response for allowlisted projects.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the upsampling path through the top_events branches (top_events > 0, both RPC and non-RPC) even though the diff adds the final_columns transformation there. A regression in the aliased column 'upsampled_count() as count' interacting with top-events orderby/limit (e.g. the RPC path's y_axes parsing of alias syntax) ships unverified; all endpoint tests use interval queries with no topEvents parameter.

[BUG] The cached branch returns `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` but the cache key hashes only project_ids, and cache.set stores a Python bool — on cache backends where cache.get returns False vs None is fine, but the key uses hash() which can return negative/colliding values and, more concretely, the eligibility result for a request with project_ids=[] is computed as False and cached under a key shared by every empty-project request in the org while _are_all_projects_error_upsampled([]) is False anyway; the actual dropped requirement is that per-dataset differences are not in the key, so the cached value from a request scoped to projects {A,B} is returned for a request scoped to projects {A,B} — safe — but for {A,B,C} if hash collides, wrong counts. Hash-colliding project-id tuples within an organization (both hash to the same int) cause a query over non-allowlisted projects to inherit the upsampled transform, inflating counts by the sample-rate factor for up to 60 seconds.

[ADVISORY] The upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered only on the discover dataset's function_converter, but organization_events_stats can route to the errors dataset (dataset == errors returns True in _should_apply_sample_weight_transform), where the 'upsampled_count()' y-axis string is dispatched to a dataset that has no such function registered. When the stats endpoint runs against the errors dataset for allowlisted projects, the transformed column 'upsampled_count() as count' is passed to a dataset whose function converter lacks the definition, producing a 400 'unknown function' (or unhandled error) for exactly the case the feature is designed for.

[ADVISORY] A git submodule pointer 'sentry-repo' is committed with no traceability to any requirement in the PR intent. Anyone cloning the repo after this merge gets an unexpected nested repo checkout (or a broken CI checkout if the submodule isn't registered), and the submodule content is invisible to review; this is accidental scope drift that ships alongside the upsampling feature.

[BUG] The diff modifies the global store_event factory to copy contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto normalized_data['sample_rate'] for every event in every test in the codebase, which is test-infrastructure behavior change unrelated to (and broader than) the stated intent of supporting upsampled error counts in the stats API. Any existing or future test that asserts on sample_rate, or whose event processing behavior depends on the absence of sample_rate, silently changes results repository-wide; this global side effect is not required by the endpoint change (the tests could construct events with the field directly) and cannot be reverted without touching unrelated tests.

[ADVISORY] The diff fixes an unrelated user-facing error message ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') that is not traceable to the upsampling requirement. Clients or tests that assert on the old error string break, and the change is unreviewed in the context it belongs to (a copy/UX fix buried in a feature PR); it should be a separate commit.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but has no caller anywhere in the diff, so the 60-second eligibility cache can never be proactively invalidated when the allowlist option changes. Operators who flip issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist off see stale upsampled (10x-inflated) counts for up to 60 seconds after disabling, with no code path to clear it; the invalidation hook is shipped inert.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling transformation is wired into only the organization-events-stats endpoint, leaving every other surface that computes count() on the same allowlisted projects (event details totals, issues list counts, org events endpoint, dashboards served by other endpoints) returning non-upsampled counts. Users on allowlisted projects see counts inflated 10x on stats charts while issue lists and event counts elsewhere show raw counts for the same query and time range, an inconsistent user experience the stated intent ('support upsampled error count') does not cover or explicitly scope out.

[ADVISORY] The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled claims it 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time' and can return different results between calls, which is false once the caller wraps it in the 60-second cache — the documented invariant the function claims to maintain is not the one the system enforces. The next engineer changing cache TTL or invalidation logic relies on the stale contract stated here and either re-introduces a fresh read where a cached one is assumed, or trusts freshness that does not exist.

[BUG] The diff commits a `sentry-repo` git submodule at the repository root pointing to an arbitrary commit a5d290951de, which is an accidental artifact and not a legitimate architectural component. Every consumer of the repo (CI, deploys, Docker builds, other devs' checkouts) now silently pulls in an unrelated nested repository, creating a parallel source path that can shadow or diverge from the real sentry code and breaks reproducible builds for anyone who does not fetch the submodule.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second cache key is `error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`, and `cache.set` is executed on every miss even for non-eligible organizations, with no bound on distinct project-tuple combinations. For the overwhelming majority of traffic (non-allowlisted orgs) every distinct project-set combination writes a `False` entry to the shared cache for 60s, flooding the cache backend with unbounded keys; additionally, removing a project from the allowlist leaves orgs serving upsampled (inflated, 10x in the test) counts for up to 60s since `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The cache layer is redundant with `options.get`, which is already cached in-process by sentry's options system, and it caches only the allowlist half of the decision while `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` is recomputed on every call anyway. The 'performance optimization' saves nothing over the existing options cache but introduces a second, manually-invalidateable source of truth for eligibility that can disagree with the live option value; the next maintainer debugging why upsampling is/isn't applied must reason about two caching layers with different TTLs.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling transform is applied only to `y_axes`/`selected_columns`; the parallel `self.get_field_list(...)`, `self.get_orderby(...)`, `equations`, and `compare_delta` paths still emit raw `count()`, so within a single top-events response the selected display fields and ordering keys use the un-upsampled count while the timeseries uses `upsampled_count()`. Users querying allowlisted projects with `orderby=count()` plus `topEvents` get rows ordered by the raw count but series values showing the upsampled count, so the displayed ordering contradicts the displayed values for exactly the orgs this feature targets.

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring match of `"event.type:error"` on the user's raw query string rather than inspecting the parsed query AST, so any query containing the literal text (e.g. `message:"event.type:error"` or a negated/complex boolean) is misclassified. A discover query filtering on a message containing that literal text against allowlisted projects gets `count()` silently replaced with `sum(sample_weight)` over mixed error+transaction rows, returning inflated/garbage counts; conversely error-focused queries expressed as `!event.type:transaction` are never upsampled.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites the exact string `count()` (case/whitespace-insensitive), leaving any other count-like aggregation (`count_unique(...)`, `count_if(...)`, `equation|count()`) untouched with no error or log. A dashboard widget mixing `count()` and `count_unique(user)` over allowlisted projects renders mutually inconsistent series — one upsampled, one raw — and the silent pass-through makes it look like the feature is working, hiding the gap from the operator who enabled the allowlist.

[ADVISORY] The only writer that derives sampling data from the `error_sampling` context (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`) lives in the test factory, while the production event pipeline's writer of `sample_weight` is nowhere in this diff — the SnQL aggregate `sum(sample_weight)` reads a column no production code path in this diff populates. Once the allowlist option is enabled in production, `upsampled_count()` sums a `sample_weight` column that ingestion never populates for real events, so charts show 0 (or null-coerced values) instead of upsampled counts for exactly the allowlisted projects; the test suite passes only because the factory fakes the writer side.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility cache key hashes `tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))` but the cached boolean is consumed for requests from all users and with all datasets/queries of that org, while the docstring in `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims fresh reads 'to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', which the surrounding cache defeats. The contradicting comments mislead the next maintainer into assuming config freshness guarantees that the 60s cache does not provide, making the safe-evacuation path (disabling the allowlist during an incident) take a minute to take effect while the docs say it is immediate.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated git submodule 'sentry-repo' is added at the repository root, pointing at commit a5d290951d. Every consumer cloning this repo now pulls an unreviewed foreign subproject; this was never part of the accepted 'error upsampling' intent and operators get an opaque dependency they cannot account for. Strongest counter (it may be a dev fixture) fails because nothing in the diff references it, so it is silent ballast.

[ADVISORY] The PR silently changes the public API error message from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1", an unrelated change smuggled into an error-upsampling feature. Any client (dashboards, SDKs, external integrations) matching or surfacing the old message text sees behavior change with no acceptance of that change in the PR's stated objective; the typo fix belongs in a separately reviewed commit.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' iteration changed the correctness contract from 'always reads latest allowlist' to 'allowlist decisions are eventually consistent for up to 60 seconds', without that semantic change being part of the accepted objective. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees up to 60s of queries where sample_weight-based 'upsampled_count()' is still applied to that project's rows; if those rows lack sample_weight the sums silently return wrong (or zero) counts for a minute after every allowlist change. The docstring itself acknowledges the two functions can disagree within one request (fresh check in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled vs cached boolean in the caller), producing inconsistent eligibility across a single user session.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but has zero call sites anywhere in the diff, so the documented cache-consistency escape hatch is unusable. When the allowlist option changes, no code path ever invalidates the 60s cache entries, so the 'eventual consistency' window is the only mechanism; a future maintainer assuming invalidation happens will be wrong. Either wire it into the option-update path or delete it (deletion test: the function, its docstring, and the cache-consistency claim all become unnecessary).

[ADVISORY] The shared store_event factory now mutates every stored event that carries contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate, setting normalized_data['sample_rate'] globally, changing fixture semantics for all existing tests that use this context. Any existing test suite that stores events with an error_sampling context (e.g. sampling-related SDK tests) now gets a sample_rate injected into its events without those tests opting in; a previously unrelated test that asserts on event data or sample_rate fails or silently produces different fixtures. Broad try/except Exception swallows the failure modes, so a broken context dict is silently ignored rather than surfacing a fixture bug.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling silently leaves every aggregation other than the exact literal 'count()' untransformed, so 'count()', 'count_unique(...)', 'count_if(...)', and aliased variants of count() in yAxis (e.g. 'count() as total') bypass upsampling while 'count()' is upsampled, producing inconsistent counts within one response. A user querying yAxis='count(),count_unique(user)' against fully allowlisted error projects gets an upsampled count() next to a raw downsampled count_unique(user) in the same response — the mixed numbers are mutually contradictory and mislead triage. The substring-based '_is_error_focused_query' has the same shape of gap: a discover query filtered via 'error.handled:false' or issue-based filters (not the literal 'event.type:error' token) is an errors-focused query that gets no upsampling. Counter-argument 'this matches the stated scope of count() only' fails because the PR title promises 'Support upsampled error count' for error queries, and partial application yields internally inconsistent data rather than merely untransformed data.

[ADVISORY] The new 'upsampled_count' SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, with a bare assumption comment that sample_weight exists for all allowlisted events, so queries routed through datasets that don't inherit this converter (or events ingested before upsampling shipped, which have no sample_weight column value) break the sum. For pre-existing events in a newly-allowlisted project, sum(sample_weight) over a column with no materialized value yields 0, so the upsampled chart flatlines for historical data while count() showed real volume — users comparing dashboards before/after the option flip see counts drop to zero. The docstring 'We rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events' states an assumption no code in this diff enforces.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check `"event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased query string, so any query that merely contains the token is treated as error-focused, including negations. A discover query of `!event.type:error` (which matches transactions/default events, not errors) contains the substring, so `count()` is replaced with `upsampled_count() as count` (sum of `sample_weight`) on a row set where sample_weight is null/absent for non-error events — Snuba returns toInt64(sum(null)) = 0 (or a query error) instead of the real count, silently zeroing or corrupting the user's chart; the same bypass works with the token inside a quoted value like `message:"event.type:error"`.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache serves a stale allowlist decision after an admin removes a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, and the companion `invalidate_upsampling_cache` cannot reliably clear it because it only deletes the one key matching the exact sorted project_id tuple the caller passes. An operator who removes a project from the allowlist (e.g., because sample_weight data is bad for it) sees up to 60 more seconds of queries rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over that project — undercounting its errors toward zero — and any invalidation call made with a different project-set combination (the common case, since queries vary the project filter) is a no-op, so the intended cache-consistency mechanism does not actually work.

[BUG] Every test in this file calls only the private helpers, so the public entrypoint is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the only function the endpoint actually invokes — including its 60-second cache-hit path, is never tested. The cached_result branch (`cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`) and the cache.set TTL behavior in src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:36-49 have zero coverage; a regression in the cache-hit path (e.g. returning a truthy string from cache, or the `cached_result is not None` sentinel colliding with a cached False being treated as a miss and re-setting) passes the whole suite while breaking the endpoint in production.

[BUG] The endpoint tests share a real (unmocked) cache across test methods keyed on organization+project_ids, so test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist asserts count==1 only if the cache entry written by test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects is absent — there is no cache.clear() in setUp, making the suite order-dependent and the assertions self-contradictory. Both tests query the same org with the same project set, so the first test caches is_eligible=True for 60s under the real Django test cache; the partial-allowlist test then reads the stale cached True, upsamples, and gets count==10 where it asserts count==1 — the suite fails (or, if the runner isolates caches per test, it silently never exercises the shared-cache behavior the code will hit in production at all).

[BUG] Patching the whole `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` module means the tests verify the mock's return value, not that the real option 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' is read with correct key or stores the type the code compares against (project IDs via `project_id in allowlist`). If the production option actually stores project slugs or is namespaced differently, every test still passes because mock_options.get.return_value is force-fed IDs, and the feature silently never activates (or crashes on type comparison) in production; nothing in the diff asserts the option name or value type against real configuration.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache, the only mechanism the module offers for cache consistency, has no tests and no call sites anywhere in the diff. Operators changing the allowlist option get 60 seconds of stale eligibility decisions with no tested or wired invalidation path; the docstring 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' is aspirational since nothing calls it and no test verifies its cache-key construction matches the read path (a key mismatch here would be silently invisible).

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling's two `except Exception: pass` branches (contexts present but not a dict, client_sample_rate present but non-numeric) are new behavior-bearing code with no test triggering either path. If normalized_data['contexts'] is a list (a real occurrence for malformed payloads), the AttributeError is silently swallowed and sample_rate is omitted with no signal; a regression that swallows legitimate errors more broadly would go unnoticed because no test stores an event with malformed error_sampling context.

[ADVISORY] test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events asserts the transaction path uses regular count(), but since _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False for the default dataset anyway, the assertion count==1 would pass even if the discover/event.type:error gating in _is_error_focused_query were inverted — the test never asserts the positive counterpart (discover + event.type:error upsampled) that would distinguish the gate from always-False. A regression that makes _should_apply_sample_weight_transform return False for all datasets (e.g. the discover import comparison breaking) passes this whole endpoint test class except the errors-dataset case, and the discover-dataset upsampled behavior ships with no end-to-end verification at all.

[BUG] The new `upsampled_count` aggregate reads `Column("sample_weight")` but nothing in this diff adds a writer or backfill that populates `sample_weight` for the discover/errors datasets, so the column is NULL for all pre-existing events. Once a project is added to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, every historical event in that project has NULL sample_weight, so `sum(sample_weight)` returns 0/NULL and the stats endpoint reports a count of 0 for all data ingested before this deploy — a silent loss of all pre-deploy error counts for allowlisted orgs with no rollback path other than removing the project from the allowlist.

[BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count() as count` based on the allowlist alone, and the docstring explicitly assumes 'the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects' — an assumption with no enforcement or backfill anywhere in the diff. Any event ingested into an allowlisted project by an older SDK (or before the sampling context existed) has no sample_weight; those events are silently dropped from counts (sum skips NULLs) instead of counted at weight 1, so customers see counts that understate errors with no error signal — silent data loss in the query layer.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))`, which is not stable across processes when PYTHONHASHSEED randomization is enabled (the default) and not stable across interpreters at all. Different workers/pods compute different keys for the same org+projects, so the shared cache (memcached/redis) never hits across workers and, worse, during an allowlist change different pods serve different eligibility decisions for up to 60s — some pods return upsampled counts while others return raw counts for the identical query, producing inconsistent dashboards mid-deploy/config-change.

[ADVISORY] The production wiring gap is masked by a test-only factory hook: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` sets `sample_rate` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only in `store_event`, while the production query path sums `sample_weight` — two different field names with no producer of `sample_weight` anywhere in the diff. The ships-inert side of the feature: only the test path synthesizes sampling data, so the endpoint-to-Snuba `sample_weight` contract is never validated against a real ingestion pipeline; the first production allowlisted org exercises the NULL-sample_weight failure mode from finding 1 rather than the intended upsampling, and any future reader of `sample_rate` on events (the field the factory actually writes) finds a column the production writer never sets.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but has no caller anywhere in the diff, so the 60-second eligibility cache is never invalidated when `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` changes. An operator removing a project from the allowlist after seeing inflated counts keeps getting upsampled (or NULL-summed-to-zero) counts for up to 60s per cached key combination; on a multi-node cache this is per-pod, so removal appears to 'not take' intermittently, prompting support escalations during allowlist operations.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring match on the query string, so any discover query containing the literal text 'event.type:error' anywhere — including a negation like '-event.type:error' or '!event.type:error', or a tag value that embeds the phrase — is classified as error-focused. A user querying discover with '-event.type:error' (transactions only, explicitly excluding errors) gets `sum(sample_weight)` applied to a result set of transaction events, for which the sample_weight column does not exist; the API either returns silently zeroed counts reported as a 200 success, or a Snuba column-not-found error surfaced as a 500 where the untransformed query would have succeeded.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to `upsampled_count()` = `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` on the assumption, stated only in a comment, that 'the database schema ensures sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects', but no such guarantee exists for events ingested before the feature rollout or by SDKs/older relay versions that never send contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate. Any allowlisted project whose error history includes pre-rollout events or events without the error_sampling context gets those events contributing 0 (or null-summing to a drop) in every stats response: the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with counts that silently undercount real event volume, with no log, no partial-result flag, and no error — the dashboard shows fewer errors than were actually received and nobody is told.

[BUG] Only the exact column string 'count()' is rewritten; any other aggregation over error events in an allowlisted project — count_unique(...), count_if(...), equations mixing count(), or 'count()' written inside a longer expression — passes through unchanged while the plain count() column on the same request is upsampled. A single stats response mixing yAxis=count() and yAxis=count_unique(user) for an allowlisted upsampled project returns one upsampled series and one non-upsampled series side by side with a 200 status and no indication they are on different scales; users comparing the two lines see internally inconsistent numbers (count=10, count_unique=1 for the same bucket) and cannot tell which is correct.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined as the documented mechanism for cache consistency ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') but has zero call sites in this diff, so the 60-second eligibility cache is never invalidated. An operator flipping `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` on or off serves stale eligibility for up to 60s (longer with cache tiering) — a project removed from the allowlist keeps returning upsampled (inflated) counts, and a project added returns non-upsampled counts, both reported as successful responses; the escape-hatch function exists but nothing wires it to the option-change path.

[ADVISORY] In the top_events path, only the timeseries columns (y_axes / timeseries_columns) are transformed to upsampled_count; the top-event selection ordering and the selected_columns (get_field_list) still run against the raw dataset, so which events are ranked 'top' is decided by raw count while the displayed series values are upsampled. Users on dashboards with topEvents for allowlisted projects get series ranked by un-upsampled count but plotted with upsampled magnitudes: a low-volume, low-sampling-rate event whose upsampled count exceeds a top-ranked event's is excluded from the top N entirely, and the top-event breakdown row shows a different (smaller) upsampled number than the total series for the same query — silently inconsistent results with a 200 status.

[ADVISORY] The 60s cache key hashes `tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))`, but eligibility also depends on the option value being org-scoped per project; two requests with the same project-id set but arriving across a mid-flight option change (or with different effective dataset/request shapes reusing the cached boolean) will get divergent answers, and the cached value short-circuits `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` only on the boolean, mixing a stale allowlist decision with a fresh per-request dataset check in the same response path. During the 60s window after an allowlist change, concurrent requests to the same org can return 200 responses where some are upsampled and others are not for the identical query, producing inconsistent charts that look like dropped or duplicated data to on-call engineers debugging an 'event count jumped' incident.

goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` only rewrites strings that normalize to exactly `"count()"` (via `lower().strip()`), and it silently passes through all other aggregations (e.g., `count_unique(...)`, `count_if(...)`, equations, etc.) with no warning/log. The diff also shows the transformation being applied broadly to `query_columns` in `organization_events_stats.py` when upsampling is enabled, so mixed yAxes could indeed result in some series being upsampled and others not, without any operator-visible indication. This is a real, diff-grounded completeness/observability concern, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect because the intended scope of upsampling in the diff appears limited to `count()` only (per the function docstring and implementation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only writer that derives sampling data from the `error_sampling` context (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling`) lives in the test factory, while the production event pipeline's writer of `sample_weight` is nowhere in this diff — the SnQL aggregate `sum(sample_weight)` reads a column no production code path in this diff populates. Once the allowlist option is enabled in production, `upsampled_count()` sums a `sample_weight` column that ingestion never populates for real events, so charts show 0 (or null-coerced values) instead of upsampled counts for exactly the allowlisted projects; the test suite passes only because the factory fakes the writer side.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new SnQL aggregate `upsampled_count()` that sums `Column("sample_weight")` (in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`) and rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` for allowlisted error queries (in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` and `organization_events_stats.py`). However, the only new “writer-side” change in this diff is test-only: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling()` in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py` sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`, not `sample_weight`. The diff does not show any production ingestion/path that populates `sample_weight`, so it’s a legitimate, diff-grounded concern that this new query behavior depends on data not demonstrated here. The finding’s definitive claim that production charts will show 0 cannot be verified from the diff alone (the writer may exist elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The eligibility cache key hashes `tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))` but the cached boolean is consumed for requests from all users and with all datasets/queries of that org, while the docstring in `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims fresh reads 'to ensure we always have the latest configuration state', which the surrounding cache defeats. The contradicting comments mislead the next maintainer into assuming config freshness guarantees that the 60s cache does not provide, making the safe-evacuation path (disabling the allowlist during an incident) take a minute to take effect while the docs say it is immediate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a 60s cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` keyed by org + project_ids (`cache.set(cache_key, is_eligible, 60)`), so allowlist changes via `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` will not take effect until cache expiry unless `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is called (no call sites shown in the diff). This conflicts with `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`’s docstring claiming it reads the allowlist “fresh each time” to reflect configuration changes during request processing, which will be false when accessed through the cached wrapper. However, the finding’s claim that the cached boolean is consumed “for all datasets/queries” is not fully accurate because the dataset/query gate `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` is still evaluated on every call even on cache hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' iteration changed the correctness contract from 'always reads latest allowlist' to 'allowlist decisions are eventually consistent for up to 60 seconds', without that semantic change being part of the accepted objective. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist sees up to 60s of queries where sample_weight-based 'upsampled_count()' is still applied to that project's rows; if those rows lack sample_weight the sums silently return wrong (or zero) counts for a minute after every allowlist change. The docstring itself acknowledges the two functions can disagree within one request (fresh check in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled vs cached boolean in the caller), producing inconsistent eligibility across a single user session.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a 60s cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (`cache.get/set(..., 60)`), so allowlist eligibility can be stale after an operator changes `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. The PR also adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` but does not wire it to any allowlist-change path in this diff, so the eventual-consistency window is guaranteed. Whether that staleness is acceptable is a product/ops semantics question (not provably a defect from the diff alone), but it is a real, diff-grounded behavior/contract change worth calling out. The finding’s claim about `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` vs cached results “disagreeing within one request” is less directly supported (the cached wrapper only calls `_are_all_projects...` on cache miss), but the core concern (stale eligibility decisions) is accurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The shared store_event factory now mutates every stored event that carries contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate, setting normalized_data['sample_rate'] globally, changing fixture semantics for all existing tests that use this context. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(normalized_data)` and calls it unconditionally inside the shared `Factories.store_event` path right after `normalized_data = manager.get_data()` (src/sentry/testutils/factories.py). This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern, though not necessarily a product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling silently leaves every aggregation other than the exact literal 'count()' untransformed, so 'count()', 'count_unique(...)', 'count_if(...)', and aliased variants of count() in yAxis (e.g. 'count() as total') bypass upsampling while 'count()' is upsampled, producing inconsistent counts within one response. A user querying yAxis='count(),count_unique(user)' against fully allowlisted error projects gets an upsampled count() next to a raw downsampled count_unique(user) in the same response — the mixed numbers are mutually contradictory and mislead triage. The substring-based '_is_error_focused_query' has the same shape of gap: a discover query filtered via 'error.handled:false' or issue-based filters (not the literal 'event.type:error' token) is an errors-focused query that gets no upsampling. Counter-argument 'this matches the stated scope of count() only' fails because the PR title promises 'Support upsampled error count' for error queries, and partial application yields internally inconsistent data rather than merely untransformed data.

adjudication.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, only the exact normalized literal `"count()"` is transformed (`if column_lower == "count()": ...`). Any semantically-equivalent count expression such as an aliased form (e.g. `"count() as total"`) or other count-based aggregations will be left untouched, meaning eligible upsampling queries can silently return raw (non-upsampled) counts depending on how the client writes `yAxis`. This creates inconsistent/broken behavior for the advertised upsampling path in `organization_events_stats.py`, which applies this transform to the `y_axes/timeseries_columns/selected_columns` just before execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'upsampled_count' SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, with a bare assumption comment that sample_weight exists for all allowlisted events, so queries routed through datasets that don't inherit this converter (or events ingested before upsampling shipped, which have no sample_weight column value) break the sum. For pre-existing events in a newly-allowlisted project, sum(sample_weight) over a column with no materialized value yields 0, so the upsampled chart flatlines for historical data while count() showed real volume — users comparing dashboards before/after the option flip see counts drop to zero. The docstring 'We rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events' states an assumption no code in this diff enforces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` which rewrites `count()` to `"upsampled_count() as count"` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py). The gating logic `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` returns `True` unconditionally when `dataset == errors`, so requests hitting the errors dataset can be rewritten to use `upsampled_count()`. However, the diff only registers the `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction in the discover dataset’s `function_converter` (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py) and does not add it to any errors dataset converter in this PR. From the diff alone, that creates a concrete mismatch: the transform can be applied for `errors` but the function is only defined for `discover`, which can lead to query-building/runtime failures for errors-dataset requests. The additional claim about historical events having no `sample_weight` values is plausible but not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check `"event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased query string, so any query that merely contains the token is treated as error-focused, including negations. A discover query of `!event.type:error` (which matches transactions/default events, not errors) contains the substring, so `count()` is replaced with `upsampled_count() as count` (sum of `sample_weight`) on a row set where sample_weight is null/absent for non-error events — Snuba returns toInt64(sum(null)) = 0 (or a query error) instead of the real count, silently zeroing or corrupting the user's chart; the same bypass works with the token inside a quoted value like `message:"event.type:error"`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_is_error_focused_query()` which lowercases the raw query string and returns True if the substring `"event.type:error"` appears anywhere (no parsing/tokenization). That means queries like `!event.type:error` or `message:"event.type:error"` will be treated as “error-focused”. When this happens (and projects are allowlisted), `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats` will transform `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count`, and `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. For non-error result sets (e.g., discover queries excluding errors), this can yield incorrect counts (0/incorrect) or errors, because the transform is applied based on a false-positive query match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache serves a stale allowlist decision after an admin removes a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, and the companion `invalidate_upsampling_cache` cannot reliably clear it because it only deletes the one key matching the exact sorted project_id tuple the caller passes. An operator who removes a project from the allowlist (e.g., because sample_weight data is bad for it) sees up to 60 more seconds of queries rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over that project — undercounting its errors toward zero — and any invalidation call made with a different project-set combination (the common case, since queries vary the project filter) is a no-op, so the intended cache-consistency mechanism does not actually work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a 60s cache in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` keyed by `(organization.id, hash(sorted(project_ids)))`. If allowlist membership changes, a previously cached `True` for that exact project set will continue to rewrite `count()` into `upsampled_count()` for up to 60 seconds regardless of the new allowlist state (`cache.get(...)` short-circuits allowlist re-check). While an `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is added, it only deletes the single key for the exact `project_ids` tuple passed, so it cannot reliably invalidate cached decisions for other project-set combinations that may have been cached (and queries commonly vary the project filter). This means cached eligibility can remain stale after an allowlist removal and continue applying the `sum(sample_weight)` transformation contrary to the updated configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every test in this file calls only the private helpers, so the public entrypoint is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the only function the endpoint actually invokes — including its 60-second cache-hit path, is never tested. The cached_result branch (`cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`) and the cache.set TTL behavior in src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:36-49 have zero coverage; a regression in the cache-hit path (e.g. returning a truthy string from cache, or the `cached_result is not None` sentinel colliding with a cached False being treated as a miss and re-setting) passes the whole suite while breaking the endpoint in production.

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test file `tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py` exercises only private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) and does not call the public function `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. The endpoint integration tests in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` will invoke `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, but only along the cache-miss path (no setup for `cache.get(...)` returning a value), so the cache-hit branch at `cached_result is not None: return cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)` is not directly covered, nor is the TTL behavior (the `cache.set(..., 60)` argument). This is a concrete coverage gap around newly introduced caching logic, not a demonstrable production defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The endpoint tests share a real (unmocked) cache across test methods keyed on organization+project_ids, so test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist asserts count==1 only if the cache entry written by test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects is absent — there is no cache.clear() in setUp, making the suite order-dependent and the assertions self-contradictory. Both tests query the same org with the same project set, so the first test caches is_eligible=True for 60s under the real Django test cache; the partial-allowlist test then reads the stale cached True, upsamples, and gets count==10 where it asserts count==1 — the suite fails (or, if the runner isolates caches per test, it silently never exercises the shared-cache behavior the code will hit in production at all).

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` writes to the real global cache (`from sentry.utils.cache import cache`) with a 60s TTL keyed only by `organization.id` and the (hashed) sorted `snuba_params.project_ids`. In the endpoint tests (`OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest`), methods patch `options.get` differently but do not clear/patch the cache in `setUp`, while issuing requests for the same organization and the same `project` set. If the first test caches `is_eligible=True`, a later test that sets a partial allowlist can still read the cached True and apply upsampling, contradicting assertions expecting regular `count()` results. This makes the test suite order-dependent/flaky under a shared in-memory test cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache, the only mechanism the module offers for cache consistency, has no tests and no call sites anywhere in the diff. Operators changing the allowlist option get 60 seconds of stale eligibility decisions with no tested or wired invalidation path; the docstring 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' is aspirational since nothing calls it and no test verifies its cache-key construction matches the read path (a key mismatch here would be silently invisible).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, but there are no call sites shown anywhere in the diff, and the new tests (`tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py` and endpoint tests) do not cover this invalidation function. The eligibility cache is set for 60s in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (`cache.set(..., 60)`), so without a wired invalidation hook, allowlist changes will necessarily have up to 60s staleness. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling's two `except Exception: pass` branches (contexts present but not a dict, client_sample_rate present but non-numeric) are new behavior-bearing code with no test triggering either path. If normalized_data['contexts'] is a list (a real occurrence for malformed payloads), the AttributeError is silently swallowed and sample_rate is omitted with no signal; a regression that swallows legitimate errors more broadly would go unnoticed because no test stores an event with malformed error_sampling context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new helper `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py` with two broad `except Exception: pass` blocks: one around `.get("contexts", {}).get(...)` and another around `float(client_sample_rate)`. This will silently ignore malformed `normalized_data["contexts"]` (e.g., non-dict) or non-numeric `client_sample_rate` and simply omit `sample_rate`. The PR also adds tests for error upsampling helpers/endpoints, but no tests exercise these exception-swallowing paths in the new factory helper, so regressions in this behavior could go unnoticed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/robustness concern, but it’s in testutils and not a clearly verifiable production defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events asserts the transaction path uses regular count(), but since _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False for the default dataset anyway, the assertion count==1 would pass even if the discover/event.type:error gating in _is_error_focused_query were inverted — the test never asserts the positive counterpart (discover + event.type:error upsampled) that would distinguish the gate from always-False. A regression that makes _should_apply_sample_weight_transform return False for all datasets (e.g. the discover import comparison breaking) passes this whole endpoint test class except the errors-dataset case, and the discover-dataset upsampled behavior ships with no end-to-end verification at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds dataset-dependent gating in `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`: always True for `errors`, always False for `transactions`, and for `discover` only when `_is_error_focused_query(request)` sees `event.type:error`. The endpoint tests cover (a) allowlisted + `event.type:error` without an explicit `dataset` parameter, and (b) explicit `dataset=discover` + `event.type:transaction` (asserting no upsampling). However, there is no explicit end-to-end test for the *discover* dataset with `query=event.type:error` to verify that the discover-specific gate actually enables the `count()`→`upsampled_count()` transformation. Because the allowlisted error test doesn’t set `dataset`, it’s not guaranteed (from the diff alone) to exercise the `discover`-specific branch, so a regression in the discover gating could go untested. This is a specific test coverage gap introduced by the new logic, not a proven functional defect in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `upsampled_count` aggregate reads `Column("sample_weight")` but nothing in this diff adds a writer or backfill that populates `sample_weight` for the discover/errors datasets, so the column is NULL for all pre-existing events. Once a project is added to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, every historical event in that project has NULL sample_weight, so `sum(sample_weight)` returns 0/NULL and the stats endpoint reports a count of 0 for all data ingested before this deploy — a silent loss of all pre-deploy error counts for allowlisted orgs with no rollback path other than removing the project from the allowlist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `upsampled_count` SnQL function that computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` (discover dataset) and rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()` for allowlisted error queries (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` + `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`). Nothing in this diff shows how `sample_weight` is guaranteed to be populated/non-null for all events that will now be queried this way, nor does the aggregation use a defensive `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)`-style fallback. However, the finding’s concrete claim that *all pre-existing events* have NULL `sample_weight` and will therefore return 0/NULL is not verifiable from the diff alone (the writer/backfill could exist elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count() as count` based on the allowlist alone, and the docstring explicitly assumes 'the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects' — an assumption with no enforcement or backfill anywhere in the diff. Any event ingested into an allowlisted project by an older SDK (or before the sampling context existed) has no sample_weight; those events are silently dropped from counts (sum skips NULLs) instead of counted at weight 1, so customers see counts that understate errors with no error signal — silent data loss in the query layer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `upsampled_count()` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to use it when `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` returns true. The implementation contains no fallback such as `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))` (or equivalent), and the docstring explicitly relies on an external guarantee that `sample_weight` exists/is populated for all events in allowlisted projects. However, the diff does not show the underlying Snuba schema/nullability or ingestion/backfill behavior for `sample_weight`, so we cannot verify from the diff alone that older/unsampled events with missing/NULL `sample_weight` actually occur and would be undercounted. What is verifiable is that the code assumes this invariant without enforcing/guarding it, which is a concrete edge-case/correctness risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(...)))`, which is not stable across processes when PYTHONHASHSEED randomization is enabled (the default) and not stable across interpreters at all. Different workers/pods compute different keys for the same org+projects, so the shared cache (memcached/redis) never hits across workers and, worse, during an allowlist change different pods serve different eligibility decisions for up to 60s — some pods return upsampled counts while others return raw counts for the identical query, producing inconsistent dashboards mid-deploy/config-change.

adjudication.rationale: In `sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, the cache key is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Python’s built-in `hash()` is intentionally randomized per-process by default (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different workers will compute different cache keys for the same `organization.id` + `project_ids`. That makes a shared cache (Redis/Memcached) effectively miss across workers and can lead to cross-pod inconsistency during the 60s TTL window after allowlist changes (some pods may serve cached eligibility from prior traffic while others recompute), affecting whether upsampling is applied and thus returned counts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The production wiring gap is masked by a test-only factory hook: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` sets `sample_rate` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` only in `store_event`, while the production query path sums `sample_weight` — two different field names with no producer of `sample_weight` anywhere in the diff. The ships-inert side of the feature: only the test path synthesizes sampling data, so the endpoint-to-Snuba `sample_weight` contract is never validated against a real ingestion pipeline; the first production allowlisted org exercises the NULL-sample_weight failure mode from finding 1 rather than the intended upsampling, and any future reader of `sample_rate` on events (the field the factory actually writes) finds a column the production writer never sets.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces query-side upsampling by summing `sample_weight` via the new `upsampled_count` SnQL function (`Column("sample_weight")` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`) and applies it by rewriting `count()` to `upsampled_count()` (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring match on the query string, so any discover query containing the literal text 'event.type:error' anywhere — including a negation like '-event.type:error' or '!event.type:error', or a tag value that embeds the phrase — is classified as error-focused. That can be applied even when the effective result set excludes errors (e.g., transactions-only), where `sample_weight` is stated to not exist, leading to Snuba column-not-found errors or incorrect results. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to `upsampled_count()` = `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` on the assumption, stated only in a comment, that 'the database schema ensures sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects', but no such guarantee exists for events ingested before the feature rollout or by SDKs/older relay versions that never send contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate.
